races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
BOYLE Sports 'Pick Your Place' Handicap

runners_data.name: Invincible Will
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile for Gavin Cromwell with Jack Kearney claiming; placed twice on good ground at seven furlongs this term and the step back from eight furlongs suits, though this steady pace may not give enough of a race to deliver a telling late run.

runners_data.name: Time Bender
runners_data.note: Won over seven furlongs on good ground last time, now returning after 264 days off for William Durkan — fitness is the key unknown but the form profile on similar going reads well and a prominent position should be accessible from the gates.

runners_data.name: Zenford
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for J P Murtagh and Ben Coen who should stroll into an uncontested lead; the style-fit flag reflects that its five-race record shows mostly placed efforts rather than wins from the front, so its finishing kick once headed is the tactical uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Dawn Romance
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up profile for M D O'Callaghan stepping up to seven furlongs after a run of six-furlong starts; the viscous headgear note and a 61-day absence are notable, and this steady pace is unlikely to generate the strong gallop that would maximise her late-running threat.

runners_data.name: Mighty Danu
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up filly for Gavin Cromwell with a win over seven furlongs on good ground in her short form profile; 58 days off since that last run is a minor query, but if she can track from midfield the flat Leopardstown straight gives her every opportunity to finish well.

runners_data.name: Dark Leader
runners_data.note: Prominent type for J A Stack with Andrew Slattery up; best run came over seven furlongs on good ground when second, and stepping back to that distance from eight-furlong efforts suits — an attainable position just off Zenford is within reach.

runners_data.name: Venetian Star
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse in nature despite being shown in midfield on the map due to redistribution — Patrick Foley's filly has placed at seven furlongs on soft ground but the faster surface and controlled tempo here work against her deepest finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Caitouna
runners_data.note: Won on good ground over seven furlongs recently for Paul Flynn and Dylan Browne McMonagle, but her natural prominent position is mapped to midfield because the race holds too many forward-going types; if she cannot access her favoured slot, her winning chance is meaningfully reduced.

runners_data.name: Watch Tower
runners_data.note: Consistent Colin Keane booking for G M Lyons; placed twice at seven furlongs on standard tracks and zero wins from five similar-going starts suggests a horse who finds a way into contention without quite delivering — but the pace map is perfectly suited to his prominent style.

runners_data.name: Chapel Lane
runners_data.note: Uncertain style (U-tagged) for W McCreery with Wayne Lordan; form figures of 373-67 show placements but no wins on good ground and the recent headgear note suggests a horse who needs things to fall right — inconsistency makes a meaningful role in any scenario difficult to project.

races.paceDynamic: Zenford is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival disputing the lead, should coast into an uncontested position from the gates and set a sustainable, unhurried gallop over Leopardstown's flat seven furlongs on good-to-firm ground. Dark Leader, Watch Tower and Time Bender are genuine prominent types who will push forward for the early positions just behind Zenford, meaning the pace is orderly rather than scorching, and the sectionals are unlikely to be truly testing. This field holds more prominent runners than the race can accommodate cleanly — Caitouna and Venetian Star are natural prominent and hold-up types respectively, but both are redistributed on the map, meaning Caitouna is unlikely to secure her favoured spot and Venetian Star's natural finishing kick from the rear may be compromised by a steady tempo that plays against true hold-up horses. A controlled, front-running gallop with a moderate pace on fast ground heavily favours horses who can sit prominently, travel through the race without expending energy, and quicken in the final two furlongs — punishing horses reliant on a strong end-to-end pace to deliver their finishing effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zenford Leads, Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Zenford is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a measured gallop, dictating every yard from gate to line.
scenarios.body: Zenford's prominent style is perfectly suited to this uncontested lead, and on good-to-firm ground over a flat seven furlongs it can quicken off its own steady pace without tying up late; horses who sit close to the action and travel smoothly will be best placed to challenge. Time Bender and Watch Tower, sitting just off the pace in second or third, are ideally positioned to pounce if Zenford's stamina fades close home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Zenford sets the pace but ties up in the final furlong, allowing a prominent tracker to sweep past.
scenarios.body: A horse like Watch Tower or Dark Leader, sitting within a length or two of the leader throughout, would have the tactical advantage of a straight run to the line with momentum already built.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Storms Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than anticipated, stretching the field and opening gaps for a horse launching from mid-division.
scenarios.body: Invincible Will has solid form on good ground and benefits from any pace injection that enables a sustained late run; Mighty Danu has won at seven furlongs on this type of ground and could find the line well from a handy midfield berth.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closer Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If a rare strong pace develops and the front end collapses in the final furlong, allowing a genuine hold-up horse to finish through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: This scenario is markedly less likely given the field's actual pace configuration and the sustainable tempo Zenford will set; Dawn Romance and Venetian Star are the most natural hold-up profiles but their chances depend on conditions that this race shape is unlikely to produce.

watchPoints.text: Zenford must be tracked from the gates — if Dark Leader or Watch Tower push forward and dispute the lead, the pace quickens and the entire race shape shifts away from a controlled front-running scenario.
Time Bender returns from 264 days off and fitness is a genuine concern; if it drops out tamely after travelling well, it could hamper horses trying to make late runs from behind.

Caitouna's redistribution is the key tactical watch — if Dylan Browne McMonagle presses forward aggressively and overrides the map position, the prominent group becomes congested and interference risk increases at the two-furlong pole.

Dawn Romance carries headgear and is stepping up in distance after a series of six-furlong runs — watch early for whether she settles in the rear or pulls too hard, as either outcome affects the hold-up scenario probability.

Good-to-firm ground confirmed for this race; monitor Venetian Star's early behaviour as any tactical effort to press forward rather than settle in her natural hold-up position would directly contradict her style-fit flag and signal a significant shift in race shape.

races.name: XIN GIN Irish EBF Brownstown Stakes (Fillies' & Mares' Group 3)

runners_data.name: Bella Isabella
runners_data.note: Weld's filly has winning form at 7f on similar ground (1/7f/SOF) and strong recent course form, but her natural racing style is front-of-field prominent; in this race she is likely to be squeezed away from that position by Duckadilly's lead, meaning she must produce her best from a less comfortable midfield berth, which tempers confidence.|

runners_data.name: Chantez
runners_data.note: Carroll-ridden four-year-old who maps genuinely prominent and is best placed to be the natural second horse in the race behind Duckadilly; headgear-fitted (blinkers) and returning after 53 days off for Lyons, whose T14 strike rate is 0/12 — the freshness angle needs monitoring alongside that cold trainer form.|

runners_data.name: Duckadilly
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who takes a drop in class and has won over a mile on Good to Firm for McLoughlin; only 11 days between runs and the STYLE_FIT flag suggests she is racing in a position that slightly overstates her tactical comfort, but here she should have the race completely on her terms from the outset.|

runners_data.name: Fingerpaint
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer partnered by Colin Keane for the in-form Weld stable (T14: 1/8), wearing a hood and stepping back to seven furlongs having shown her best form over that trip with a win at 7f/Good; needs enough pace from Duckadilly to make ground into, and the Good to Firm ground is no concern.|

runners_data.name: Nancy J
runners_data.note: Ben Coen-ridden hold-up filly for Murtagh, who has been active (T14: 4/19) and ran just 12 days ago; her OR of 83 makes her the bottom weight here and she faces a stiff task against this quality, though her 3/8f/GOO run shows she can place when conditions suit her off-the-pace style.|

runners_data.name: Phenomenal Filly
runners_data.note: Twomey's three-year-old returns from a 285-day layoff having won at 7f/Good last season, and her true inclination is to race up with the pace — in this field she is pushed toward a midfield mapping that doesn't reflect how she naturally operates, so the fitness question after nearly ten months off compounds the positional disadvantage.|

races.paceDynamic: Duckadilly is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival prepared to contest the lead, she should coast into an uncontested early position and set a sensible, self-regulated gallop on Good to Firm ground over seven furlongs at Leopardstown. Fingerpaint and Nancy J are the true hold-up operators who will track from the rear and rely on a strong enough pace to close into, while Chantez will try to slot in prominent behind Duckadilly. This field holds more prominent-leaning types than the race shape can accommodate: Bella Isabella and Phenomenal Filly are both natural front-runners pushed into midfield positions in the map because Duckadilly is likely to control the pace alone, meaning neither will be racing in their natural rhythm. With a single uncontested pace-setter likely to control tempo from the front and create a sustainable rather than blistering gallop, the race shape most strongly favours a horse who can settle just off the pace and produce a well-timed run, rather than pure hold-up closers who need a truly strong pace to reel the leader in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Duckadilly Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Duckadilly leads without any prominent rival pressuring her and sets a comfortable, controlled gallop that she can sustain to the line.
scenarios.body: Duckadilly dictates from the front at a pace entirely of her choosing on fast ground she handles well, and without any horse willing to challenge her lead she can conserve energy through the first half before quickening in the straight; this scenario strongly benefits horses who can sit just behind the pace and challenge at the two-furlong pole, rather than those closing from far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Get Late Momentum
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough through the middle portion that hold-up horses get a genuine tow into the race and the leader ties up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Fingerpaint, the most credentialled hold-up performer in the field with a Weld/Keane combination at peak confidence, swoops from off the pace if Duckadilly's gallop proves quick enough to string the field out; Nancy J, though on a lower mark, also has the profile to finish powerfully if the race is run to suit her late style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Bella Isabella or Phenomenal Filly manage to secure a closer-to-pace position than the map suggests and produce their best form from that spot.
scenarios.body: Both horses are naturally front-running or prominent types who, if the pace distribution loosens slightly at the start, could slot in directly behind Duckadilly in their true racing position; Bella Isabella's winning form over seven furlongs on similar going and Weld's strong trainer-14 return of 1/7 give her a genuine chance if she recaptures that spot.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Tactically
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is too slow and the race turns into a sprint from the two-furlong pole, favouring pure speed over stamina or positioning.
scenarios.body: A muddling tempo that suits neither closers nor a controlling leader can produce a blanket finish where a sharp, tactical sprinting type wins on natural acceleration; Chantez and Phenomenal Filly, who both possess turn-of-foot when not ground down by strong gallops, are best placed to capitalise on a truly falsely-run race.

watchPoints.text: Duckadilly — watch the pace she sets from the front; if McCullagh allows her to coast through the first three furlongs unchallenged, the race tempo may be too slow for any hold-up horse to close, rendering Fingerpaint and Nancy J passengers.

Bella Isabella and Phenomenal Filly at the start — both are natural prominent types and there could be a positional scramble in the early strides as they attempt to claim ground behind Duckadilly that the race map cannot fully accommodate.

Fingerpaint's hood (headgear flag) — first-time or returned headgear at Leopardstown over a trip she has handled before is a positive angle, but if it affects her manageability in the early stages it could compromise Keane's ability to hold her back correctly.

Chantez — 53 days off and trainer Lyons returns 0/12 in the last 14 days; the freshness and cold trainer form together are worth discounting slightly despite her having the natural position in this race to exploit the anticipated pace shape.

races.name: Harry Meighan Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Glyndwr
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose two recent wins came over 8f at Sligo on Standard ground; similar-going record modest (0W2P from 10 tries), but the handicapper has him at OR 82 and Nicola Burns's 5lb claim adds value if she can deliver the horse late.|

runners_data.name: Ocean Manifest
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning after 111 days off — trainer Thorne hits 1/6 over the past 14 days suggesting horses are in form; will likely dictate from the outset but the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.92 hints at questions about whether this is fully its race shape.|

runners_data.name: Bill Silvers
runners_data.note: Absent 301 days and last three turf runs in similar going produced no placing (0W0P from 15 sim-going starts); Harry Eustace yard 0/2 in the 14-day window — significant fitness and form questions surround this reappearance.|

runners_data.name: Dark Viper
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a blinkered headgear; sim-going form reads 1W4P from 9 runs on Good, suggesting it handles the surface, though recent finishes of 0-6-8-8-5 suggest a horse looking for conditions to fall right rather than one in peak form.|

runners_data.name: Heliogabalus
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 8f on Good at what appears a similar level, and the form string (3-1-0-0-1) shows a pattern of bouncing back; Colin Keane's booking is a sharp upgrade in ride quality and this horse's going record (2W4P from 11 on Good) is the most compelling in the prominent group.|

runners_data.name: Dark Summit
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — five consecutive finishes of 17th, 12th, 10th, 10th, 8th with a tendency to drop out once the race quickens; Denis Hogan's yard is 3/18 in 14-day window but this horse's profile screams against in a tactical finish.|

runners_data.name: Eddie G
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer wearing a tongue-tie; sim-going record 0W2P from 5 on Good and has placed three times at this level over 7f-8f; Adam Caffrey takes the ride and the step back to 8f from recent outings could sharpen the finish.|

runners_data.name: Zaraahmando
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery, which is an unusual dynamic; tongue-tied and with two wins in the form book at 8f on Good, the sim-going record (2W5P from 11 on Good) makes this one of the better course-and-distance profiles in the race.|

runners_data.name: Frank Pickle
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by nature but redistributed to midfield given the volume of closers in the field — his best form came over 10-12f at Listowel and Leopardstown on yielding ground, and the drop back to 1m on Good to Firm with the likely map position all point against Ben Coen finding his best work.|

runners_data.name: Finsceal Annie
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-held-up performer wearing a tongue piece and a pads; recent form 8-11-15-6-2 suggests inconsistency and she has been better over 8f at the Curragh on Standard; Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking brings significant jockey quality to a horse whose form otherwise merits modest expectation.|

runners_data.name: Hamiyan
runners_data.note: Three-year-old stepping into a handicap off OR 77 on a career sim-going record of 0W0P from 1 start on Good; D K Weld's patient yard (1/7 in 14 days) and the 81-day absence make this an intriguing but uncertain proposition — the absence of any similar-going evidence is a concern.|

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose last five runs include recent 5th-5th finishes on Good at 8f; redistributed to midfield as the back of the field is overcrowded, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 the horse is unlikely to find its natural position — Hogan's yard has two winners in the 14-day window but the race shape does not suit.|

runners_data.name: Ballymagreehan
runners_data.note: Won over course and distance (8f Good, Leopardstown) two starts back, showing course form that stands out; a natural prominent type redistributed to midfield on the map due to field density, but Ballymagreehan is the most likely of the displaced horses to force its way forward — the 0.93 STYLE_FIT tag reflects positional risk rather than a fundamental mismatch.|

runners_data.name: Heart Of Eternity
runners_data.note: Career form of 14-14-8-6-13 suggests a horse struggling at this level; a true hold-up runner placed into midfield on the map given rear overcrowding, and with 109 days off and a STYLE_FIT of 0.90, the Hogan yard's 1/26 recent run rate compounds the concern — hard to find a strong angle here.|

races.paceDynamic: Ocean Manifest is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only one horse willing to lead from the front, is likely to enjoy a largely uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop on this Good to Firm Leopardstown mile. The pace will be genuine but controlled — Ocean Manifest sets the fractions from the front, and without a significant challenger for that position, the speed is unlikely to become truly punishing. Heliogabalus, Dark Viper, Eddie G, Zaraahmando and Finsceal Annie will press for prominent berths just behind the leader, creating a compact early order, while Glyndwr, Hamiyan and Dark Summit track from midfield to rear. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can naturally secure their preferred positions — Ballymagreehan, Frank Pickle, Liberate and Heart of Eternity are all redistributed on the map, and of those Ballymagreehan is the most likely to actually force its way into a prominent pitch given its recent win over course and distance. The tactical verdict is clear: a single front-runner dictating a moderate-to-honest pace on fast ground strongly favours prominent racers who can travel just off the lead and quicken from there — hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to make ground are disadvantaged, particularly the redistributed types who will not find their natural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Ocean Manifest sets a fair but uncontested pace and the prominent group tracks comfortably before unleashing a finish from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Ocean Manifest draws the race along at an even tempo, and horses like Heliogabalus, Zaraahmando and Dark Viper, travelling just off the pace, are perfectly positioned to pounce entering the straight on this flat track. Good to Firm ground rewards horses with a clean action who can quicken from a handy position rather than those grinding from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Denies All
scenarios.trigger: If Ocean Manifest is permitted to dictate fully uncontested, sets a deceptively slow early pace and kicks clear at the 2f pole before rivals can close.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to pressure Ocean Manifest in the early stages, it controls tempo absolutely and conserves enough energy to sprint clear late, its 111-day absence freshened rather than rusty given trainer Thorne's recent 1/6 form. The flat Leopardstown configuration and Good to Firm surface suit a front-runner who can sustain its gallop, though the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.92 does temper confidence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Delivers Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Ocean Manifest sets a stronger-than-expected gallop and the race develops at a pace quick enough to compromise the prominent horses' finishing kicks.
scenarios.body: A genuinely fast early tempo would string the field out and leave true hold-up horses with the freshest legs in the straight, allowing Glyndwr, Hamiyan or Frank Pickle to reel in tired rivals. However, with multiple redistributed closers unlikely to find their natural rearward slot, and the pace projected as moderate, this scenario carries reduced probability — the hold-up horses may not get the strung-out race they need.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles The Form
scenarios.trigger: If a slow early gallop causes a bunched, messy finish in which positional chaos and bumping compromises fancied horses.
scenarios.body: With 14 runners on a mile track and multiple prominent types fighting for position, a falsely-run race could see interference disrupt the fancied runners' finishing runs and open the door for an unconsidered horse to benefit from a clear run. Dark Summit's tendency to fade, Ocean Manifest's fitness query and the compressed pace bands all add to the unpredictability element in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Ocean Manifest's 111-day absence combined with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 means its ability to control the race over a full mile on return is unverified — if it gets headed or outpaced from the front, the race shape collapses quickly.

Heliogabalus and Zaraahmando are both prominent types who will compete for the same early position just off Ocean Manifest — any scrimmaging between them in the first two furlongs could compromise one or both at a critical stage.

Ballymagreehan has genuine course-and-distance form and is likely to push forward despite being mapped to midfield — if it successfully secures a prominent berth, it becomes a legitimate factor that the race shape projections may underweight.

Dark Summit is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish and has five consecutive poor performances; W J Lee on board gives it tactical options but if it gets into a prominent position and stops, it could cause significant interference in a tight 14-runner field.

Good to Firm going at Leopardstown is confirmed across all races on the card — any horse with a sim-going concern or whose best form came on softer surfaces (Bill Silvers, Frank Pickle, Hamiyan) should be monitored in the betting in case market support suggests connections have private going confidence that the public form book does not reflect.|

races.name: Double First Stables Irish EBF Nasrullah Handicap (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: Diego El Queso
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here with Colin Keane aboard for Lyons' yard, which is in strong 14-day form; last run was 85 days ago and he goes on good-to-firm, but the STYLE_FIT tag suggests he is racing somewhat out of his most comfortable role and has only managed 0W3P on similar ground, which tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Lord Massusus
runners_data.note: Sam Coen (5lb claim) partners this hold-up type for Joseph Murphy, whose yard has a modest 14-day record; has placed at this level on good ground before (9/15 on similar) and a genuinely fast pace would suit, but recent form figures of -86367 are hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Cloud Seeker
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this prominent type who has excellent recent course form at 1m-plus on good ground, boasting 3W6P from 15 similar-going runs; handles this trip well but needs a smooth passage from a prominent berth to show his best.

runners_data.name: Retracement
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides for JP Murtagh, whose yard has a solid 5/27 in the last 14 days; wears headgear (p) and has shown he handles good ground over 10f, winning last time, though drops back in trip slightly here and his 2W3P on similar ground reads reasonably.

runners_data.name: Slieve Binnian
runners_data.note: David Marnane's six-year-old is a genuine front-runner by nature but the map has had to push him back — there are simply too many prominent types ahead of him and he is unlikely to find his natural position, making the STYLE_FIT discount (0.93) meaningful; his recent form of -50069 is difficult to upgrade on.

runners_data.name: Playin Cool
runners_data.note: John James Feane's four-year-old wants to race prominently but with the pace map full, he faces the same positional squeeze as several others; 0W2P from 7 runs on similar going and recent form 1-8023 suggests he has ability but has struggled to reproduce his best consistently, and his yard has a blank 14-day record.

runners_data.name: Jamestown
runners_data.note: The three-year-old is progressive, posting three consecutive placed or winning efforts including a win, and Luke McAteer rides for the in-form Marnane yard; has shown tactical versatility and handles good ground over 7-8f, stepping up to 9f here for the first time which is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Harana
runners_data.note: D K Weld's four-year-old is listed with headgear (p) and last won over 10f on good ground, showing he stays and acts on the surface; his best profile is as a prominent type who can quicken, and a faster tempo caused by the compressed field would play to his strengths — modest 14-day yard record of 0/5 noted.

runners_data.name: Nakasero
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's five-year-old wears tongue-tie and hasn't run for 55 days, returning after a break; his best form has come over 10-12f on cut, and the step down in trip on fast ground creates a concern — 1W1P from 15 similar-going runs reflects the ground question, and the redistribution from his natural prominent position further complicates his race.

runners_data.name: Thread Of Gold
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan partners Willie Mullins' lightly-raced three-year-old who won over 7f on good ground last time; has run only three times, giving this progressive sort an improving profile, and 1W2P from just three similar-ground runs means the sample is small but the quality reads well for a horse stepping into handicap company.

runners_data.name: Harmani
runners_data.note: G M Lyons' three-year-old wants to race prominently but has been pushed back on the map given the congestion; he won last time over 10f on good ground and has solid placed form on soft, so the surface is fine — the redistribution and STYLE_FIT discount (0.92) mean he may not get the run of things, though raw ability makes him one to track.

runners_data.name: Anvika
runners_data.note: Rory Cleary rides Sheila Lavery's hold-up type who wears a tongue-tie; recent form figures of -80033 show she has found a rhythm of placing without winning, and 0W4P from 15 similar-going runs tells a consistent but unspectacular story — she needs the pace to collapse to give her a chance of getting competitive late.

races.paceDynamic: Diego El Queso is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push him, will stride into an uncontested lead from the front, setting a controlled, honest gallop over this 1m1f on good-to-firm ground at Leopardstown. The pace map identifies Harmani, Slieve Binnian, Playin Cool, Nakasero, and Harana as true prominent types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field cannot physically accommodate them all in their natural position — in reality, several will press forward and create a more competitive early tempo than the lone-leader tag implies, with Cloud Seeker, Jamestown, Retracement, and Thread Of Gold also likely to sit close to the pace. This compression of prominent runners behind Diego El Queso means the early and middle sections will be busier than a single front-runner race normally produces, generating a pressured, honest tempo that will draw the pace out of the prominent brigade and open the race up for those who settle cleanly through the middle stages. The tactical verdict is clear: horses with a genuine ability to travel smoothly just off the pace in a medium-sized field, conserve energy through the turn, and quicken over a stiff final furlong on fast ground are most favoured — the efficient prominent-to-midfield settler who can produce a sustained finish is the profile to focus on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Diego El Queso leads at a fair tempo and the jostling prominent runners settle into a rhythm without excessive early burning.
scenarios.body: Diego El Queso dictates at a sustainable clip, the pack strings out naturally behind him, and the horse who travels best just off the lead has first run into the straight with enough in reserve to hold on; the good-to-firm surface rewards those who keep a forward position without over-committing early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Lifts Closers
scenarios.trigger: If multiple redistributed prominent types — Harmani, Slieve Binnian, Playin Cool — push hard early and force an above-average tempo that burns out the leaders.
scenarios.body: A stiffer-than-expected gallop results in the forward runners tying up in the straight, and the handful of genuine hold-up or settling types who absorb the pace find themselves with a clear, energy-efficient run to the line; Lord Massusus and Harana, who have the ability to quicken late, would benefit most from this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Diego El Queso — despite carrying 140lbs and racing somewhat out of natural style — is allowed a soft, unchallenged lead and the prominent pack fails to close the gap through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to go with him, Diego El Queso controls the fractions entirely, preserves his energy, and Colin Keane times a controlled acceleration that the chasing pack cannot match on a flat, fast track; his recent win form and Lyons' strong 14-day strike rate support this as a genuine, if secondary, possibility.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Three-Year-Olds Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace scenario suits the less exposed three-year-olds who are potentially ahead of their current mark and produce a big performance on good-to-firm ground.
scenarios.body: Jamestown and Thread Of Gold — both three-year-olds with progressive form and experience on similar ground — find themselves racing at a faster tempo than their older rivals handle, and their relative freshness and improving profile carries them clear late; this scenario depends on the tempo genuinely stretching the field rather than producing a falsely-run finish.

watchPoints.text: Jamestown and Thread Of Gold are both three-year-olds with progressive profiles and have the potential to be ahead of their marks — watch whether they travel smoothly in the first half of the race, as either producing a big performance on good-to-firm ground would not be a surprise.

Multiple redistributed prominent types — Harmani, Slieve Binnian, Playin Cool, Nakasero — cannot all get their natural front-end position; watch the early stages for jostling and any horse that burns energy fighting for position, as those that do are significantly less likely to finish strongly.

Diego El Queso has been off 85 days and is carrying 140lbs as the nominal front-runner — if he shows any signs of flattering early and dying in the straight, the race could unravel quickly for those committed to chasing him.

Cloud Seeker's trainer-jockey combination (Andrew Slattery) is unusual and warrants monitoring for any market drift or support before the off, given his strong course-and-distance form figures of 3W6P from 15 similar-going runs suggest he is well placed on paper.

Harana's headgear (p) and D K Weld's typically patient placement of horses means his recent win over 10f on good ground may be more relevant than it appears — watch where Chris Hayes positions him early, as any prominent move could signal confident yard intentions.

races.name: Mervue Equine Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Burford Beauty
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who has struggled to recapture her best, with only one placed run in nine recent starts on similar ground; 41 days off and a step up to 9f here make this a tough ask from deep in a 25-runner field.

runners_data.name: Mullacurry Maid
runners_data.note: True hold-up mare with a flagged tendency to fade late; only one run on similar going in four starts and that was a fifth of seven, making her profile unconvincing at this trip and in this race shape.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who shaped best over shorter good ground, placing twice over 8-9f; Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking adds interest but the horse has faded in five of seven recent starts and the step beyond a mile looks stretching.

runners_data.name: Anchors Away
runners_data.note: Hold-up gelding trained by Quinn who has placed at 10f on good ground but repeatedly fades; the 5lb claimer Paddy Harnett takes off useful weight, though the horse has not won in his last five and tends to find only one pace.

runners_data.name: Max Meridius
runners_data.note: Thomas Mullins-trained hold-up horse who has been racing almost exclusively at 16f and has now dropped back dramatically in trip; the form profile at this sort of distance on good ground is shallow and the style mismatch is significant.

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has placed twice at 9f on good ground; Denis Hogan's yard has 2 from 11 over 14 days and J M Sheridan takes the mount, but repeated fading in the straight limits confidence from this position.

runners_data.name: Not Simple
runners_data.note: Hold-up gelding with a 51-day break and poor going profile; has only raced on heavy or soft-ish surfaces recently and the good-to-firm conditions here represent a significant unknown in terms of comfort.

runners_data.name: Slaney Swagger
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare trained by Melia who has placed five times without winning, including a third and a second at 8f on good-to-firm ground; the course-form profile is modest but the going suits better than most in this section.

runners_data.name: Shelbourne Flyer
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's mount is a natural hold-up performer who has been moved into midfield on the map due to the overcrowded rear — Keane's tactical sharpness gives him the best chance of any redistributed horse of actually manoeuvring into a useful position from which his good-ground 7f form can translate over this extra distance.

runners_data.name: Nibras Rainbow
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner; won over 8f on good ground at this course and races from a good draw, giving Leigh Roche the option to dictate every yard from the front; his style_fit flag reflects that his role is singular rather than genuinely contested, but that is a strength in this race more than a weakness.

runners_data.name: Shahada Ace
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery rides his own horse; a hold-up type placed out of position on the map, as the field has too many closers for the map to accommodate naturally — despite one win, the form profile shows ten finishes of sixth or worse in recent similar-going starts and the style compromise is significant.

runners_data.name: Sayfa Fad
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's 5-year-old has one win at 8f on good ground and was moved to midfield on the map from his natural hold-up berth; the fade flag and a form string showing a 14th and 13th on recent good outings dampen confidence even when repositioned forward.

runners_data.name: Alto Sax
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the mount on Fahey's 5-year-old who has won twice on good and good-to-firm surfaces; his natural closing style has been mapped to midfield due to field congestion, but the horse has shown tactical flexibility and the Fahey-Coen combination is potent — the style displacement is real, but he remains of interest.

runners_data.name: Yquem
runners_data.note: Richard Brabazon's 4-year-old won at 9f on good ground last time and has prominent form mixed in with his hold-up tendencies; Chris Hayes is an astute jockey who could exploit this horse's versatility if positioned near the pace from the outset.

runners_data.name: Morning Approach
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up type who has failed to win in his last five and repeatedly finishes mid-division; mapped away from his natural rearmost position due to field volume, and the fade flag is a persistent concern at his age.

runners_data.name: Famous Enough
runners_data.note: Prominent-style gelding who finished second over 8f on good ground and has placed three times in his last seven; Luke McAteer is a capable judge of pace and this horse's profile — sitting just behind the sole front-runner — suits the expected race shape well.

runners_data.name: Folk Warrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up gelding who has been racing at 12-16f and has now dropped to 9f; the distance shortfall combined with repositioning away from his natural style makes this a speculative entry, though the going is not a concern.

runners_data.name: La Campanella
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who wears a hood and has placed twice at 8f on good ground; mapped out of her natural rearmost position and has a repeated fade pattern late, which limits her prospects even if repositioned into midfield.

runners_data.name: Lady Crossing
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with a fade flag and a form string showing a best of fourth at 8f on soft going; the step up in trip and the good-to-firm conditions are both moves away from her comfort zone based on recent evidence.

runners_data.name: Milverton
runners_data.note: 7-year-old hold-up gelding who wears headgear and ran a placed sixth at 8f on good ground; Karl Thornton's horse has been mapped to midfield from his natural rearmost position — the consistency of mid-division finishes without a win in recent form is the defining feature.

runners_data.name: Quarry Stone
runners_data.note: A 2-year-old listed — age designation appears anomalous for a horse with handicap form — who has been absent for 273 days; the very long layoff combined with consistent finishing positions in the 12-14 range on good ground make this a very difficult race on return.

runners_data.name: Half Nutz
runners_data.note: 9-year-old who has placed twice recently at 9f and 7f on good ground, showing genuine consistency without winning; mapped out of his natural hold-up berth but James Barcoe's gelding does at least have multiple top-3 finishes in similar conditions.

runners_data.name: Rushford
runners_data.note: Hold-up gelding who wears a hood and has placed in a 9f good-ground contest; the fade flag and a form string of 9th, 15th, and 9th on similar surfaces limit enthusiasm, even accounting for the weight concession from the low OR40.

runners_data.name: Jazz Dreamers
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a 160-day absence and a form profile dominated by Dundalk and Thurles; the return from a lengthy break and the absence of meaningful good-ground form at this trip make him a difficult proposition in a wide field.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: Hold-up gelding who has placed at 8f on good-to-firm and has Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim to assist; mapped out of his natural rear position, but the recent consistency — three top-8 finishes in his last five — gives him at least a base level of relevance.

races.paceDynamic: Nibras Rainbow is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 25-horse field and, with no genuine pace rival pressing from the off, is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m1f at Leopardstown on good-to-firm ground. Famous Enough is the only other prominent-style runner capable of tracking the leader, meaning the pace band ahead of the field will be thin and the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching. With the gallop manufactured rather than contested, the race sets up for horses who can travel prominently and produce a finish, rather than for true hold-up closers who need a strong pace to chase down. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Shelbourne Flyer, Shahada Ace, Sayfa Fad, Alto Sax, Yquem and others are genuine come-from-behind horses who have been redistributed into midfield positions they will not naturally secure; the two who are most likely to actually land prominent ground are Shelbourne Flyer, given Colin Keane's ability to find cover and position, and Alto Sax, who has shown tactical versatility. The tactical verdict is clear: a single front-runner dictating a moderate pace on good-to-firm ground at a flat track strongly favours prominent or prominent-tracking horses who can produce an extended finish without needing a fast early pace to set them up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nibras Rainbow Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Nibras Rainbow leads without serious early challenge and the pace remains modest, allowing prominent horses to travel within themselves.
scenarios.body: Leigh Roche can dictate every yard at a sustainable clip, meaning horses who can sit just off the pace — Famous Enough, Shelbourne Flyer if Keane gets him into a better spot — travel comfortably and strike before true hold-up types can engage. On good-to-firm ground at Leopardstown, the premium is on horses who travel smoothly in the first three to four positions and have a clean turn into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Sweeps Past
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and a prominent-tracking horse produces a decisive move two furlongs out before Nibras Rainbow can quicken.
scenarios.body: Famous Enough, having finished second on similar ground, can sit just behind Nibras Rainbow and deliver a challenge that the front-runner, already at a flat-out tempo, cannot repel; this shape suits horses with a finish at this trip rather than pure closers. Yquem, who won over 9f on good ground and has been ridden prominently before, could also emerge strongly if positioned in the first four through the early exchanges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Redistributed Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly quicker than expected and a redistributed hold-up type finds a clear run through the compressed midfield to deliver a late challenge.
scenarios.body: Shelbourne Flyer with Colin Keane, or Alto Sax with Ben Coen, are best placed of the horses mapped out of their natural position to find the gaps in the straight on a flat track that doesn't blunt momentum; neither is a true closer in this race shape, so this depends on the pace being quick enough to uncoil them. The flat Leopardstown straight gives a brief window for a late sweeping run, but with only one front-runner this scenario requires near-perfect execution from a compressed field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Nibras Rainbow sets a sufficiently measured pace that no rival can overhaul and Leigh Roche times a late injection of pace to perfection.
scenarios.body: On good-to-firm at Leopardstown over 1m1f, an uncontested front-runner with a recent win over this course and distance combination is a live threat to simply outstay a disorganised hold-up field who never find clear running; Nibras Rainbow's recent course win over 8f good gives strong evidence he handles the conditions. This scenario is dampened by the rating step-up he faces off his OR52, but a fully uncontested lead is never a trivial advantage in a 25-runner handicap.

watchPoints.text: Nibras Rainbow — watch whether Leigh Roche is challenged for the lead in the first furlong; if he goes entirely unchallenged, the front-runner's advantage in a 25-horse field on good-to-firm will be very significant.

Famous Enough — watch his early position; if Luke McAteer slots him directly in behind Nibras Rainbow within the first two furlongs, he becomes the most naturally placed horse to capitalise on the expected race shape.

races.name: Hurling For Cancer Research Supported By Centra On July 24th (Q.R.) Race

runners_data.name: Delta
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's hold-up type arrives on a sharp 13-day turnaround with P W Mullins aboard; his sim-going form (1W3P on good) and natural rearward style fit the expected race shape precisely, with the compressed field likely to suit a late-finishing burst from off the pace.

runners_data.name: The Mediator
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's nine-year-old showed useful recent form (1-3-3 in last five) and handles good ground well, but his instinct to race prominently means he is squeezed into a midfield berth here — his effectiveness will depend on whether he can find a cleaner path than his natural position allows in this crowded pace picture.

runners_data.name: Sirius
runners_data.note: A 261-day absence is a significant flag for W P Mullins' gelding, and while he has won over comparable trips on good ground, the long layoff combined with being pushed back from his preferred prominent berth makes him a difficult proposition to rely on; his jumping record and class are the only reasons to keep him in mind.

runners_data.name: Catalani
runners_data.note: Jack Foley's OR-120 performer steps back to 1m7f having competed at marathon distances (22-25f), and his solid sim-going record (1W2P in 3-4 starts) suggests the quicker surface is no issue; the drop in trip may sharpen him up and he is realistically the best-placed horse to sit just behind Murat.

runners_data.name: Friary Road
runners_data.note: Returning after 336 days off (and 70 jumping days), T M Walsh's six-year-old has a decent course record (won over 1m6f on good) but the extended absence and the fact that his prominent style is squeezed out of position in this field combine to make this a speculative reappearance at best.

runners_data.name: Murat
runners_data.note: Peter Lawlor's confirmed front-runner has a strong record on good-to-firm and similar going (3W3P in 7 starts), and his role as sole pace-setter over this trip is straightforward; the STYLE_FIT flag is noted — if the pace is too comfortable he becomes vulnerable to a late burst — but he controls the race's tempo completely.

races.paceDynamic: Murat is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a six-runner field, he will stride into a soft, uncontested gallop from the gates over this 1m7f trip on good-to-firm ground at Leopardstown. The pace he sets will be honest rather than searching — a solo leader rarely stretches a field on good ground over a staying trip, meaning the race will be run at a comfortable rhythm that keeps the tempo manageable for those tracking him. Sirius, The Mediator, and Friary Road are all natural prominent racers but the map cannot accommodate all three in their preferred positions, so Catalani — higher-rated and fresh — is the most likely to actually slot into the one slot just behind Murat, with the redistributed trio forced wider or deeper than they would like. This shape — a controlled, uncontested lead with a compressed field behind — strongly favours hold-up horses with a clean turn of foot to unwind late, and notably Delta, who sits back naturally and whose profile aligns perfectly with a race where the pace is honest but not punishing.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Murat Dictates, Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Murat leads unchallenged and the pace stays measured, creating a steadily-run staying contest.
scenarios.body: Murat controls from the front at a fair but unextravagant clip, keeping the field together into the straight, where the compressed bunch sets up a decisive late burst from a quality hold-up horse. Delta, racing from off the pace as is natural, has the profile to pick them off once the race truly ignites in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Breaks Free
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent types manages to secure a position close to Murat and sustains the effort through the straight.
scenarios.body: With pace pressure from a secondary challenger, the race develops into more of a true test of stamina, stretching the field and rewarding a horse with genuine staying class at the head of affairs. Catalani, whose form over big distances on good ground is solid, is best placed of the prominent types to capitalise if the tactical picture clears.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Staying Test Grinds Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens in the back straight and turns this into a genuine stamina examination from an early stage.
scenarios.body: A gruelling tempo would expose lighter-weighted or less-genuine stayers and reward those with deep reserves over the 1m7f trip. Sirius has shown he can stay and has won over similar distances, while Delta's class gives him residual claims even in a true slog.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Left Flat-Footed
scenarios.trigger: If Murat presses home a long-range run from the home turn and the tracking horses are caught cold.
scenarios.body: A front-runner who gets soft fractions and then lifts the tempo at the right moment can steal a race on good ground before hold-up horses can respond. Murat's 1m6f win on good ground shows he can see out the trip and quicken, making him the beneficiary if the field dawdles until it is too late.

watchPoints.text: Murat sets the fractions entirely alone — watch whether H C Swan opts for a genuine pace or a dawdle, as it dictates whether this is a true staying test or a sprint finish.
Sirius returns from 261 days off for W P Mullins; a fit-again bounce run is possible but the lack of recent race fitness is a live concern in a competitive amateur riders' heat.
Friary Road has been absent 336 days (70 jumping days) — watch in the parade ring for signs of condition and freshness before drawing any conclusions about his readiness.

The three redistributed prominent types (Sirius, The Mediator, Friary Road) will jostle for the one available tracking position behind Murat — monitor early running to see which actually secures it, as that horse gains a meaningful tactical advantage.
Catalani drops sharply in trip from 22-25f chase distances back to 1m7f — watch whether the shorter test brings more pace and freshness or catches him out positionally before he can settle.
